plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. With rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below your true value. However, since the values are discrete, and the increments are $0.1, I should bid slightly below my value to avoid overpaying. Given my value of $25, I will bid $24.9.

This is a single-round auction. The optimal bidding strategy in a sealed-bid second-price auction is to bid truthfully. This is because bidding less than your value risks losing the auction when you could have won and made a profit, while bidding more than your value risks winning the auction and paying more than the item is worth to you. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

This is the first round, so I have no history to learn from. Since all bidders are rational, the optimal bidding strategy is to bid slightly below your value. However, I don't know the other bidders' values. A good starting point is to bid a fraction of my value, say 80%, to ensure a positive expected profit if I win. This also allows me to gather information about the other bidders' bidding behavior in future rounds.
